text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
-- Prime Minister Lionel Jospin to face on Tuesday first test of his electoral campaign promises to press for alternative solutions to a planned shutdown of the Renault Vilvoorde assembly plant.
-- European partners hope to reach agreement on European monetary stability pact at Amsterdam meeting next week.
-- Sommer-Allibert Canadian subsidiary Domco attracts interest from U.S. investors.
-- European Monetary Institute chairman Alexandre Lamfalussy repeats need to announce foreign exchange rate parities when decision made on which which countries can join single currency.
-- France calls for a European monetary stability pact that takes employment issues into account.
-- European fund managers bet on a soft euro, according to a survey for Merrill Lynch.
-- Mobile telephone market soared in France in May with 250,000 new subscribers.
-- Rumours of Casino's interest in Promodes intensify.
-- Union sources expect a six-month delay in the planned shutdown of the Renault Vilvoorde plant.
-- Finance and Industry minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn is quoted as saying he expected "positive results" about Renault Vilvoorde plant to come out of today's Renault shareholders meeting.
-- France will not be ready to ratify European stability pact next week, asks for more time and stronger measures against unemployment.
